Ah, Rocket League. I actually love this little gem. I had heard over the past few months abut how this is really addictive, and having bought it on sale a few weeks ago, I can see why. I've already racked up over 30 hours in the time I have to spend on gaming (which is split between this and MGSV TPP), but it's really, really fun. Like, seriously.

Rocket League, essentially, is IS football (or soccer for the US of you) with RC cars. It's simple, it's easy to grasp, and it's probably the biggest draw. For an arcade game, there's no need for complicated mechanics. It's literally 'drive your car into the ball'. Sure, there's some tact, like purposefully hitting a specific area of the ball to send it in a certain direction (aka Rule 101 of soccer), but it's simple enough for anyone to understand.

There's 2 main modes - Online, and Season - and they're pretty self-explanatory. Season mode is where you play with an AI team (or none, if you're going 1v1) for the title. You pick a logo, a team name, and play against a team of equal number at a set difficulty ("Rookie", "Pro", and "All Star"), although the first two settings I find too easy. 'All Star' actually gives some challenge which is never a bad thing. There's other settings, to,o, including how many teams are in the playoffs, and what your AI team look like, but it's fairly irrelevant for the most part.

Online is where the game really comes into it's own, as you're obviously playing against other people. Headsets/Mics are supported, so you can communicate more effectively with your team if you so choose, but for a light-hearted party game it's pretty much unnecessary. There's a few 'quick comments' you can give ('Great shot!', 'What a pass!', 'Good save!' etc), although at least for the PC version, you can type your own messages. Crossplay is supported with the PS4, which just shoots home how console friendly it is. Any driving game is better with a controller than a keyboard (I use a wired 360 controller), so I highly recommend you pick one up if you're on PC. There's also a fair amount of customization, carying from different shades of colour, to what's on the end of your antenna, to your rocket trail. These are unlocked via levelling up, which is a fairly simple task - just score goals or do special moves when you're playing (saving goals, clearing the ball etc).

That said, the novelty could be seen as quick to wear off. I played the game virtually exclusively for about 2 weeks before I continued my progress in MGSV, but that's not to say it's not fun. It's just that there's not much beyond the bread and butter of RC car soccer, which I feel is the only main selling point. It's worth picking it up if you haven't already - just to see what the fuss is about - but if you do, I'd grab it on sale.

I haven't paid for any of the DLC, but from what I can tell it's purely cosmetic; as far as the what you see with the core gameplay is concerned, whta you see is what you get. I remember reading something about the developers creating some new style arenas (I imagine platforms etc) to spice up the gameplay, but you'd have to check that out for yourself.

5/10: The game is bursting with colour, along with some slick controls, neat customization options, and a concept that anyone can get a hold of, but the lack of lasting appeal is Rocket League's biggest downfall, not to mention the slightly high entry fee. Definitely worth grabbing on sale with a few friends, but it's too much of a 'been there, done that' affair to have any real lasting effect.
